messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx rate detected for service=model-serving-prod (us-west1). Start=2025-11-03T17:02:01Z. Error mix: 502, 503, timeouts. Recent surge correlated with heavy long-seq requests. Paging on-call.
anya: I'm oncall — looking. Do we have a primary error class? segfaults/ooms/connection resets?
marco: seeing lots of 502/503 in gateway logs. A subset of runners returning 5xx with exit code 139 (SIGSEGV) and some OOM kills. Also evictions reported on nodes: kube evict loop for pods with high RSS.
eli: adding tracing link -> https://internal.traces/redwood/trace/0xabcde (note: restricted)
anya: good catch. Initial hypothesis: KV cache growth + long context causing memory pressure and eviction oscillation under parallel requests. Can we throttle long-seq clients and route to fallback pool?
sre-manager: agree. Steps: 1) Apply circuit-breaker on /v1/generate for requests > 4k tokens. 2) Reroute traffic to reserved-dedicated pool (if capacity). 3) Respawn affected nodes with kernel param tweak for oom_adj. Who can flip circuit-breaker now?
marco: can do the routing. Pushing a traffic rule to route heavy-seq requests to model-compact-1 and reserved-pool-usw. Doing slow roll.
ops-bot: deploy start: /ops/route apply --filter "tokens>4000" --to reserved-pool-usw
ops-bot: deploy complete: 1798760028
anya: temporarily enable fallback model variant (quantized) for legacy clients. Marco, how many requests matched the filter so far?
marco: ~320 req/min matching >4k tokens during the spike, peak 1100 req/min overall. After route change 20% of those still hitting original pool due to stale connections.
eli: evict logs from node-37:

```
[kubelet] Evicting pod model-runner-7bf: memory pressure RSS 42GB > limit 36GB
[oom_kill] kill_process: pid 23456, name model-runner, oom_score_adj=0
[signal] process exited with signal 11
```
anya: can we cordon node-37 and reprovision? Meanwhile enable retry-window at gateway to avoid immediate fail-through.
marco: cordoned node-37 and drained. Spinning up replacement with kernel swappiness tweak: vm.swappiness=10 and userland cgroup mem limit enforcement. New nodes coming up.
customer-success: customer-impact: we've got a handful of customers reporting 5xx in us-west1 (approx 15 impacted workspaces). Notifying top 5 with ETA ~30m for mitigation.
anya: add temporary global rate-limit on large payloads, reduce parallelism at runtime for model-runner (max_concurrency -> 2 for heavy requests). Patching config now.
ops-bot: apply config patch: model-runner.max_concurrency_heavy=2
ops-bot: patch applied: 1798760055
eli: collecting core dump from crashed runner for postmortem. Core located at s3://cores/usw/node-37/core. Will attach to incident ticket.
marco: after routing + concurrency cap we're seeing 5xx rate drop from 42% -> 9% over 3m. Latency improved for small requests. Heavy queue still has occasional timeouts.
anya: good. Next: 1) keep routing rule for 1h, 2) repro on staging with KV cache stress test, 3) plan driver fix for cache eviction heuristics, 4) customer comms.
sre-manager: assign owner for postmortem and follow-up: eli for root cause analysis, marco for runtime config changes, anya for KB + customer updates.
customer-success: sending initial notice to affected customers (short blurb + mitigation steps). Will track responses.
eli: quick note — core shows repeated null deref in attention kernel when sequence > 6k tokens with cached-shard enabled. Attaching stack snippet in ticket.
anya: ok. Once spike stabilizes to <5% for 15m we can close pager. Keep updates here. If error rate resurges, re-escalate to infra.
marco: monitoring dashboards -> error rate trending down. Keeping reserved-pool warm for 45m.
ops-bot: monitor alert cleared at 1798760088
anya: closing the immediate mitigation. Postmortem owners assigned. Thanks team :thumbsup:
sre-manager: filing incident ticket with tags: runtime-segfault, memory-pressure, evictions, routing-mitigation. Follow-up meeting scheduled in 24h.
customer-success: update sent to customers at 17:12 UTC.
